  "answer": "When an `interrupt()` is called, LangGraph saves the graph state using its persistence layer, effectively checkpointing execution. Upon resuming the graph with `Command({ resume: ... })`, the node where the interrupt occurred re-executes from its beginning. This re-execution means that any side effects or operations that occurred before the `interrupt()` call within that same node will also run again. If these prior operations are not idempotent (meaning they can be safely executed multiple times without unintended consequences), this can lead to issues like duplicate data creation or unexpected state changes, thus not guaranteeing exactly-once side effects."
